About 475 cells do not fit the pages: Malwa (200 cells; the page never names Malwa as a Yadava conquest, Simhana's 1215 invasion and Krishna's victory before 1250 are raids), Lata (147; captured only in 1220), the north of the Tungabhadra (83; the Hoysalas held it to the Malaprabha and Krishna until about 1212) and Kolhapur (63; annexed about 1216). The ledger adds Kolhapur back in 1216, the Hoysala land in 1212 and Lata as a vassal in 1220-1232.

keyframe_review.note: 446,850 km2 for 1236-1259. The Singhana II page puts the north limit at the Narmada ('it probably extended up to the Narmada River'), the south at the Tungabhadra, the west at the Arabian Sea and the east in 'the western part of Andhra'; Malwa lies north of the Narmada, and Lata was lost after the peace of c. 1232. Kolhapur and the Hoysala north stay Yadava. Repair pass: Cliopatria's 1236 shape lacks 117 of the 200 cells of the 1212 gain and 69 of the 132 cells of the 1216 gain, so about 186 cells (some 47,000 km2) would have vanished at 1236 with no loss event; the union keeps them, as the Singhana II page has the conquest north of the Tungabhadra completed by 1220 and records no later loss.

The 1236-1259 shape holds to 1313 apart from the ledger: northern Konkan joins in 1265, the Kakatiya lobe leaves in 1294 and Ramachandra's north-eastern conquests join in 1308. Cliopatria's 1260 Yadava shape (484,133 km2, 1,966 cells) is NOT followed where no page supports it: its Chhattisgarh (230 cells), Jabalpur and Madhya Pradesh (152) and eastern Vidarbha lobe (about 96,000 km2), which the Ramachandra page (r. c. 1271-1311) gives only as undated conquests of Tripuri (Tewar near Jabalpur), Vajrakara (probably Vairagad) and Bhandagara, are drawn by the 1308 ledger gain at three radii (the page names no Chhattisgarh place at all, so Chhattisgarh is not drawn); its Navsari/Lata fringe (30 Gujarat cells; the Navsari jagir is after 1308 and a grant to a refugee) and about 60 cells of the Karnataka coast (Uttara Kannada and Goa) have no page; the 99 cells of the Kakatiya lobe that no Yadava shape holds are not Yadava here (kakatiya-dynasty draws them from nobody). The Konkan is drawn from 1265 (see the ledger) instead of 1260. No infobox km2 to compare (the Seuna infobox gives none).

keyframe_review.note: Repair pass. Cliopatria's raw 1314 shape (483,759 km2) holds the 16 Malwa cells that the earlier keyframes trim, the Navsari/Lata fringe, the Karnataka coast and the Chhattisgarh lobe, none of which a page supports, so they would have returned at 1314 with no event. This shape is the earlier keyframe carried through the ledger (1265 Konkan, 1294 loss of the Kakatiya lobe, 1308 north-eastern gain) and is 1,636 cells (about 414,000 km2) against Cliopatria's 1,965 (about 497,000 km2): 481 cells are out (the Chhattisgarh lobe beyond the three radii, the Navsari fringe, the Karnataka coast, Malwa) and 152 are in (the radii beyond Cliopatria's outline and a strip of the Tapti valley that Cliopatria drops in 1260). The years change: Cliopatria runs the row to 1325 but the dynasty ends in 1317. Delhi governs the land from 1313 to 1315 (Kafur) and again from April 1317; the ledger draws the interlude of Harapaladeva's independence.

region.text: Devagiri and the former Chalukya capital Kalyani

ledger.note: c. 1187: Bhillama V founds the Yadava kingdom of Devagiri. 'Around 1187, Bhillama forced Ballala to retreat, conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani'; 'He then established Devagiri, a formidable natural stronghold, which became the new Yadava capital.' The infobox says 'Established: c. 1187'. Cliopatria's row starts in 1188.

region.text: Kalyani (Basavakalyan) and the former Chalukya capital district

ledger.note: c. 1187: Bhillama V takes Kalyani from the Western Chalukyas ('conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani'). The page describes no battle against the Chalukya armies; the western-chalukya-empire dossier records the matching 1187 loss.

region.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side

ledger.note: late 1180s: the Hoysalas push the Yadavas north. 'In the late 1180s, Ballala launched a campaign against Bhillama, and decisively defeated his army at Soratur'; the Yadavas were pushed north of the Malaprabha and Krishna rivers. The page gives no year, so 1188 is the opening bound (page silent; confidence 1); the end is dated c. 1191 by the Veera Ballala II page. The hoysala-kingdom dossier dates the battles of Soratur and Lakkundi c. 1191 from the Veera Ballala II page.

region.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side

ledger.note: c. 1191: the Hoysalas win at Soratur and Lakkundi and hold the land north to the Malaprabha and Krishna. 'In c. 1191, the Hoysala monarch gained the upper hand over Yadava Bhillama V in the critical battles of Soratur and Lakkundi' (Veera Ballala II page); 'By c. 1189, Basavakalyana had fallen to Bhillama V'. The Seuna page has the Soratur defeat only 'in the late 1180s' and says the Malaprabha and Krishna 'formed the border for the next two decades'; hoysala-kingdom has c. 1191, and the end of the contest now agrees with it. The Yadava base shape leaves the Hoysala-held land out until 1212.

region.text: the Yadava-Kakatiya frontier of the Telangana marches

ledger.note: c. 1194: the Yadava Jaitugi invades the Kakatiya country. The Seuna page: Jaitugi invaded around 1194 and forced them to accept Yadava suzerainty. The front is not named, so the zone is the frontier band.

region.text: the Yadava-Kakatiya frontier of the Telangana marches

ledger.note: 1198: the Yadavas install Ganapati as a vassal. The Singhana II page dates Jaitugi's appointment of Ganapati to 1198 and says Mahadeva was killed and Ganapati was installed as a Yadava vassal; the Kakatiya dossier's pages (Ganapati Deva) have Mahadeva dying in 1198-1199 and Ganapati ruling in his own right from 1199, so the vassalage is drawn as the vassal events below (Singhana II page, confidence 2).

region.text: the Kakatiya kingdom of the day: the Telangana core, since no page dates a wider extent before 1199

ledger.note: 1198: Jaitugi makes Ganapati his vassal. 'Jaitugi is known to have appointed the Kakatiya ruler Ganapati as his vassal in 1198' (Singhana II page); the Seuna page has Jaitugi force Kakatiya acceptance of Yadava suzerainty about 1194. The Ganapati Deva page (kakatiya-dynasty) has Mahadeva killed in 1198-1199 and Ganapati released in 1199 and says nothing of a vassalage.

region.text: Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga, Shimoga and most of Dharwad

ledger.note: 1212: Singhana II takes the land north of the Tungabhadra from the Hoysalas. The page: by 1212 the Yadavas had reached Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga and Shimoga, by 1213 they had annexed most of Dharwad, and the conquest north of the Tungabhadra was completed 'By 1220'. The hoysala-kingdom dossier has the matching c. 1212 loss. Anantapur, Chitradurga and Shimoga are places the Yadavas had 'reached' (inscriptions or raids, not stated annexations) and are not drawn; Anantapur and Chitradurga are not in the gazetteer's place list.

1216: Singhana II annexes the Kolhapur kingdom. Around 1216 Simhana II defeated Bhoja II; 'The Shilahara kingdom, including its capital Kolhapur, was annexed.' The Singhana II page has Bhoja fleeing to Panhala and the annexation before 1217.
1220: the Yadava general Kholeshvara invades Lata. The page: Lata was captured in 1220 by Kholeshvara and given to Shankha as a vassal. The chaulukya-dynasty dossier draws the same contest from 1220.

1220: Lata is given to Shankha as a Yadava vassal. The Singhana II page: Shankha was captured, then released as a Yadava feudatory. The Seuna page says Simhana appointed Simha's son Shankha, the Singhana II page Sindhuraja's son; he is a Yadava vassal, not a Chaulukya feudatory, so the counterpart is listed as a state needing a dossier.

region.text: the Kakatiya kingdom of the day: the Telangana core, since no page dates a wider extent before 1199

ledger.note: c. 1231: Ganapati becomes independent. 'During the second half of his reign, Ganapati seems to have assumed an independent status' and the page records no major conflict between the two kings or any date for the change. Ganapati reigned c. 1199-1262, so the middle of the reign, 1231, is a bridge (page silent; confidence 1).
c. 1232: peace with the Chaulukyas. 'The Chaulukya-Yadava conflict came to end in c. 1232 with a peace treaty.' The page adds that Lata was later lost to Lavanaprasada's invasion (undated).
c. 1232: Shankha's Lata passes out of Yadava hands. The page dates the loss to Lavanaprasada's invasion only as 'later'; the 1232 peace is the bridge (page silent; confidence 1).

region.text: northern Konkan, the Shilahara country with its capital at Thane

ledger.note: c. 1265: the Yadavas take the northern Konkan. The Shilahara dynasty page lists the North Konkan Shilaharas as 'c. 800-1265 CE', capital Thane, the last ruler Someshvara 1255-1265, 'subdued by the Yadava ruler Singhana II around the beginning of the 13th century'; the Seuna page has Mahadeva (r. c. 1261-1270) curb 'a rebellion by the Shilaharas of northern Konkan' under Someshvara, and a Kadamba rebellion put down 'around 1268'. No page calls it an annexation or dates it, so the year of the line's end is a bridge (confidence 1) and the vassalage from the early 13th century is not drawn. Cliopatria's Yadava shape already holds 139 of the 221 Konkan cells from 1188 and 1236; the earlier draft gained the Konkan in 1260 on no page.

ledger.note: 1294: the Kakatiyas take Raichur. The page: in 1294 the general Vitthala-deva-nayaka built fortifications at Raichur; after 1296 the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra 'annexed the eastern part of Ramachandra's kingdom, which included the present-day Anantapur and Raichur districts.' The kakatiya-dynasty dossier (Prataparudra II page) dates the Raichur Fort inscription 1294 and Gona Vithala's capture of forts in Bellary district and the Raichur Doab. The region is Cliopatria's 1260 transfer to the Kakatiyas. Repair pass: the loss is restricted to the cells this dossier holds; about 50 further cells of Cliopatria's lobe (Nellore and the Kadapa country excluded) were in no Yadava shape and kakatiya-dynasty draws them from nobody.

1296: Alauddin Khalji, governor of Kara, raids Devagiri. 'In 1296, Ala-ud-din Khalji of the Delhi Sultanate successfully raided Devagiri' while Simhana was away; Ramachandra agreed to a treaty and tribute. The tribute relation is for the khalji-dynasty dossier's vassal events.
1296: the raid ends with a ransom and annual tribute. The page gives no month and no land ceded.

1307: Alauddin sends Malik Kafur against Devagiri. 'In 1307, Alauddin decided to invade the Yadava kingdom of Devagiri'; the infobox dates the Siege of Devagiri 1308 and the Ramachandra page dates the campaign 1308.

1308: Ramachandra submits. Kafur 'easily subjugated the Yadavas'; Ramachandra was taken to Delhi, where he acknowledged Alauddin's suzerainty. The Ramachandra page has him reinstated with the title Raja-i-Rajan and Navsari as a jagir. No land annexed.

region.text: the north-eastern conquests of Ramachandra: Tripuri, Vajrakara and Bhandagara (Ramachandra page); the place names stand in as radii

ledger.note: 1271-1308: Ramachandra extends the kingdom to the north-east. 'He occupied the former Kalachuri capital Tripuri (modern Tewar near Jabalpur)', 'subjugated the rulers of Vajrakara (probably modern Vairagad) and Bhandagara', and the Purushottamapuri inscription 'suggests that he expanded the Yadava dominion at its north-east frontier' (Ramachandra page, r. c. 1271-1311). The page dates none of these, and the Seuna page has him sovereign only to 1308, so 1308 is the latest bound (confidence 1); the radii stand in for the three named places. 'Former' Kalachuri capital: the Kalachuris of Tripuri are no longer a state, so the counterpart is nobody. Cliopatria's Chhattisgarh lobe is not drawn: the page names no place there.

region.text: the Yadava kingdom at its end

ledger.note: 1317: the Yadava dynasty ends at Devagiri; the Seuna page has it 'annexed by the Khalji sultanate in 1317'. Daulatabad is the later name Muhammad Tughluq gave the city.

wars.name: Seuna conquest of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bhillama V conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani and founded Devagiri.

wars.name: Hoysala victory at Soratur

zones.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side

wars.outcome: Ballala's Hoysalas decisively defeated Bhillama at Soratur and pushed the Yadavas north of the Malaprabha and Krishna.
wars.note: The Veera Ballala II page has c. 1191 for the battles of Soratur and Lakkundi and c. 1189 for the fall of Basavakalyana to Bhillama V; the Seuna page says 'the late 1180s'; hoysala-kingdom has c. 1191.

wars.name: Jaitugi's Kakatiya war
wars.outcome: Jaitugi invaded about 1194 and forced Yadava suzerainty; in 1198 Mahadeva was killed and Ganapati installed as a Yadava vassal (Singhana II page).
wars.note: The Kakatiya Ganapati Deva page has Mahadeva dying in 1198-1199 and Ganapati ruling in his own right from 1199. The vassalage of Ganapati (1198, until the second half of his reign) is in the ledger from the Singhana II page.

wars.name: Singhana II's conquest of the northern Hoysala land

union.text: the Karnataka land north of the Tungabhadra up to the Malaprabha and Krishna, Dharwad and Belgaum side

zones.text: north of the Tungabhadra and Bellary

wars.outcome: By 1212 the Yadavas had reached Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga and Shimoga; by 1213 most of Dharwad; the conquest north of the Tungabhadra was completed by 1220 (the Hoysala page of the hoysala-kingdom dossier says after c. 1212).

wars.name: Yadava invasion of Malwa
wars.outcome: Simhana II invaded in 1215 and defeated Arjunavarman; Krishna defeated the Paramara king before 1250 and Ramachandra defeated the Paramara army in the 1270s; no annexation is recorded.

wars.name: Conquest of the Kolhapur Shilaharas
wars.outcome: Simhana II defeated Bhoja II, who fled to Panhala; the kingdom including Kolhapur was annexed about 1216.

wars.name: Yadava invasions of Lata
wars.outcome: Kholeshvara captured Lata in 1220 and Shankha ruled it as a Yadava vassal; a joint invasion with Paramara Devapala failed; peace about 1232; Visaladeva's invasion of Gujarat in the 1240s failed.

wars.name: Mahadeva's invasion of the Kakatiya kingdom
wars.outcome: Mahadeva invaded the eastern Kakatiya kingdom and was apparently repulsed; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The Rudrama Devi page (kakatiya-dynasty) dates the Kakatiya general Bhairava's defeat of the Yadava army 'probably in or after 1263'.

wars.name: Ramachandra's northern wars
wars.outcome: Ramachandra defeated the Paramara army in the 1270s, fought the Vaghelas inconclusively (the Thane and Cintra inscriptions each claim a win), occupied Tripuri (undated) and subdued Vajrakara and Bhandagara (undated); a Varanasi temple suggests he held the city for 2-3 years in 1286-1290 (Altekar), which Joshi calls 'totally hollow'.
wars.note: Repair pass: the three named conquests are drawn by the 1308 ledger gain (undated, confidence 1).

wars.name: Yadava-Hoysala war of 1275-1276
wars.outcome: Tikkama invaded in autumn 1275; the Hoysala forces were defeated in January 1276; on 25 April 1276 Ankeya Nayaka led a decisive attack and Tikkama retreated to Dhummi; no border moved.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of the Raichur Doab

zones.text: the land Cliopatria moves from the Yadava shape to the Kakatiya shape in 1260: the Raichur Doab, Bellary, Gulbarga and Bidar side, Kurnool and the Rayalaseema side, a strip of western Telangana

wars.outcome: Vitthala-deva-nayaka fortified Raichur in 1294; after 1296 Prataparudra annexed the eastern part of Ramachandra's kingdom, including the Anantapur and Raichur districts.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Devagiri
wars.outcome: Alauddin raided Devagiri in 1296 for ransom and tribute; Malik Kafur subjugated Ramachandra in 1307-1308; after Simhana III's revolt Kafur annexed Devagiri in 1313; Harapaladeva restored Yadava rule until Mubarak Shah's campaign of April 1317 ended it.
wars.note: The Seuna page dates the annexation 1317 and the lead 1308; the Malik Kafur page dates it 1313.

certainty.note: Yadava frontiers rest on inscription find-spots and claims; no treaty line is recorded. The Narmada and Tungabhadra are the page's northern and southern limits at the height under Simhana II; the Lata frontier after the peace of c. 1232 is undated.

sources.title: Seuna dynasty
sources.note: Identity, 1187 Kalyani and Devagiri, wars and conquests by reign, Khalji invasions, end 1317; no km2 figure. Repair pass: Shankha of Lata a Yadava vassal; ruler years (Bhillama V c. 1187-1191, Jaitugi c. 1191-1200/1210); Mahadeva curbs the northern Konkan Shilaharas; the 'late 1180s' Soratur defeat; Harapaladeva c. 1313-1317.

sources.title: Singhana II
sources.note: Reign, Hoysala land by 1212-1220, Kolhapur, Lata, extent (Narmada to Tungabhadra), the 1198 appointment of Ganapati. Repair pass: Ganapati appointed vassal in 1198, independent in the second half of his reign.

sources.title: Ramachandra (Yadava dynasty)
sources.note: Reign 1271-1311, 1270s Paramara and Vaghela wars, Hoysala war 1275-1276, Raichur 1294, Khalji tribute; Navsari jagir. Repair pass: Tripuri, Vajrakara and Bhandagara undated; Malwa invaded in the 1270s (Paithan inscription 1271); Chhattisgarh not mentioned.

sources.title: Malik Kafur
sources.note: 1307-1308 and 1313 campaigns against Devagiri; annexation of 1313.

sources.title: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah
sources.note: Harapaladeva's independence and the April 1317 campaign; governor Malik Yaklakhi.

sources.title: Veera Ballala II
sources.note: Soratur and Lakkundi c. 1191; Basavakalyana to Bhillama V by c. 1189; Hoysala frontier at the Malaprabha and Krishna.

sources.title: Shilahara dynasty
sources.note: North Konkan Shilaharas c. 800-1265, last ruler Someshvara 1255-1265, 'subdued by the Yadava ruler Singhana II around the beginning of the 13th century'.

notes:
See history/polities/_notes/sa-03-h.md. Cliopatria's Yadava row (1188..1325) is corrected in five ways: it starts a year after the c. 1187 founding; the 1188-1259 shapes include Malwa and Lata, which the pages do not give the Yadavas, and the Hoysala-held north of the Tungabhadra and Kolhapur before their conquests of about 1212 and 1216; the 1260 shape moves the Raichur Doab and the Kurnool side to the Kakatiyas 34 years before the 1294-1296 events the pages date; the row runs eight years past the dynasty's end in 1317; and the interlude 1313-1316 (Delhi annexation, then Harapaladeva) is carried by the ledger. Unverified: the Chhattisgarh and Jabalpur lobe of the 1260 shape, the Konkan coast, the Gujarat fringe (Navsari was granted to Ramachandra in 1308 per the Ramachandra page), and the whole of the Yadava vassalage of the Kakatiyas (1198) and the Delhi tribute (1296-1313), which the khalji-dynasty and kakatiya-dynasty dossiers should carry. Bhillama V's and Jaitugi's reign years are not on the pages opened, so the ruler strip starts in 1210.

Repair pass 2026-10-19 (reviewer: fail). K2 (1236) is now the union of Cliopatria's 1236 shape and the 1212 and 1216 gains (without Malwa and Lata), so no cells vanish at 1236. K3 (1260) no longer follows Cliopatria's 1260 shape: the Chhattisgarh, Jabalpur and eastern Vidarbha lobe is trimmed and returns by the 1308 ledger gain at the three places the Ramachandra page names (Tripuri, Vajrakara, Bhandagara; undated, confidence 1; Chhattisgarh itself is on no page), the 99 cells of the Kakatiya lobe that no Yadava shape holds are no longer Yadava, and the Navsari/Lata fringe and Karnataka coast are not drawn. K4 (1314) is the same kingdom carried through the ledger instead of Cliopatria's raw 1314 shape (which brought Malwa back). Thin items acted on: the Konkan gain moves from 1260 to 1265 on the Shilahara dynasty page (last North Konkan Shilahara ruler 1255-1265; the same page has the Yadavas subduing the line 'around the beginning of the 13th century'); the Hoysala contest ends c. 1191 (Veera Ballala II page; the Seuna page says 'late 1180s'); Ganapati's vassalage is drawn 1198-c. 1231 (Singhana II page; end is a bridge); the ruler strip starts with Bhillama V (1187) and Jaitugi (1191). 'Shankha of Lata' is listed as a counterpart needing a dossier. Kept: the Seuna lead says Devagiri was annexed in 1308 and the body 1317 (the page is inconsistent); the 1316 restoration under Harapaladeva stays a confidence-1 bridge (the Seuna page lists his reign c. 1313-1317 and does not describe the restoration). The Ramachandra page says Ramachandra invaded the Paramara kingdom in the 1270s and the Paithan inscription of 1271 'alludes to his conquest of Malwa'; no annexation is recorded, so Malwa stays out of the shape.
